Base directory for this skill: <HOME>\repos\wiki-master-worktrees\five-skills\skills\wiki-maintainer

# Maintaining the wiki

Select the requested mode; read [access](references/access.md) and only the
references relevant to that mode. Treat `` as the request when the host
has not substituted it.

- **Health, structural defects or backlog counts:** [health](references/health.md)
  and [metrics](references/maintenance.md). Reporting does not process clippings.
- **Freshness and what needs factual review:** [freshness](references/stale.md).
- **Consistency, contradictions, unsupported quotes and factual fixes:**
  [lint](references/lint.md) and [evidence](references/evidence.md).
  For quotation-pairing and style-flag mechanics, read the
  [content lint contract](../../README.md#content-lint).
- **Broken citations or integrity worklist repairs:** [repair](references/repair.md).
- **Useful relationships, forward links, orphan navigation and task maps:**
  [relink](references/relink.md) and [identity and relationships](references/efficacy.md).
- **Clipping failures, fidelity flags, declines and human decisions:**
  [triage](references/triage.md). Presenting the UI creates only local session
  state; applying dispositions is a separate action. Before applying re-clips or
  quarantine, read [re-clipping and quarantine](../../docs/reclipping.md).
- **Native Obsidian mechanics when a maintenance step needs them:**
  [Obsidian commands](references/obsidian-cli.md). Requested app actions also
  route here from wiki-user; ordinary file work does not require the app.

Health, freshness and preview reports do not open operations, log, commit or
refresh indexes. Before applying authorized changes, read
[evidence](references/evidence.md) and [operation completion](references/operations.md).
Keep reports distinct from mutations; a request for a report does not authorize
repairs. Preserve raw bodies and foreign edits, validate the actual changed
paths, and finish scoped publication unless the user holds it. Purge keeps its
separate plan and publication approvals in [wiki-purge](../wiki-purge/SKILL.md).

A clean graph does not prove factual accuracy. During substantive maintenance,
use cheap structural checks and a bounded review of changed or high-use pages;
skip an empty vault and avoid a full lint of an unchanged wiki. Preserve factual
review dates on mechanical edits and report coverage limits. For cross-mode
orientation only, see the [workflow overview](references/workflows.md).
Mode is triage. I'll read access.md and triage.md.

# Vault access and host commands

Resolve the plugin root from the installed `SKILL.md` location, not the current
working directory: its containing skill folder's `../../` is the plugin root.
From a file in a skill's `references/` folder, use `../../../` instead.
Resolve and quote absolute helper paths before running commands. Treat
`$ARGUMENTS` as the user's request when the host has not substituted it. A linked
skill or reference can be read directly when the host has no skill loader; shared
policy does not require loading the maintenance-role entry point.
Resolve `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` (default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; with `WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` set and no vault named, a script stops with exit 2 instead of using the default) and verify the expected
vault layout. Read local `AGENTS.md` and schema before edits. A known root and
filesystem access are sufficient for the supported operations below; do not ask
the user to restart Obsidian as a prerequisite for all work.

## Layout and read scope

`raw/clippings/` holds captured evidence; `wiki/{sources,entities,concepts,syntheses,authored}/`
holds maintained pages; `moc/` holds navigational maps; `log/` holds one file per
operation. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it. Reads do not
open operations, write logs, commit or refresh indexes. Before any authorized
mutation, read [operation completion](operations.md); before quoting or
synthesizing, read [evidence](evidence.md).

Prefer bounded search and relevant MOCs to the generated catalog. Search
diagnostics describe coverage, not relevance: a stale index can omit useful pages.
Read current passages and disclose weak or failed channels. Index freshness is
distinct from factual review dates.

## Choose the supported channel

| Operation | Channel and fallback |
|---|---|
| Read a Markdown page or source | CLI `read path=...`, or read its exact path under the known vault root. |
| Search | Prefer `search.mjs` and inspect its diagnostics. If a channel fails, use available results plus bounded filesystem `rg` over `wiki/` and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/` only for evidence lookup. State missing channels. |
| Health, evidence routes, identity, relationships, drift coverage | Bundled filesystem helpers work without Obsidian. Do not gate them on `assertRunning`. Drift embeddings still require their backend. |
| Factual freshness report | `stale.mjs` may use CLI discovery or scoped filesystem fallback. Preserve missing-review and coverage diagnostics. |
| Ordinary Markdown creation/editing | Use exact-path filesystem edits even when the CLI is healthy, with the same operation, evidence, schema and validation contract. Read current content before editing; preserve unrelated changes. Never pass a whole note body through `content=`. |
| Small typed property or app actions | Use the guarded CLI entry point below; filesystem property edits remain available with schema validation. |
| Opening a note in the UI, executing an Obsidian/plugin command, app state, live Bases queries | Requires working Obsidian CLI. Report the specific unavailable action; continue independent file work. Do not pretend a filesystem approximation executed an app action. |

For CLI calls use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" <command> ...`
or the bundled `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. These share an OS-managed lock across
agent processes, vaults and plugin copies for the same user. Do not launch native
`obsidian` directly or bypass a busy guard; other tools' raw calls are not protected.
The guard waits up to 10 seconds for a turn, then fails without sending a request.
Command execution has its own 10-second default timeout. Each request is limited
to a conservative 2,048-byte UTF-8 JSON envelope and rejects physical CR/LF/NUL.
This policy is not Obsidian's documented maximum. If rejected before sending,
use filesystem Markdown editing or narrow the read query; do not split a note
into many CLI writes or disable the guard. No fallback performs writes implicitly.
After an unavailable CLI or timeout, choose the supported fallback once; never
loop waiting for the app. **A timed-out mutation has an uncertain outcome.** Read
the exact target and check the intended effect before retrying or switching to
filesystem writes. An exit or timeout alone does not establish that nothing ran.
OS cleanup releases a lock after process death, but cannot prove a surviving CLI
child or an already-submitted Obsidian mutation finished. Inspect uncertain targets.

Validate resolved paths stay under the known root. Restrict searches to explicit
content directories; exclude `.recycle/`, dot folders, dependency trees and binary
originals. Do not recursively enumerate the entire user profile or scan a recycled
topic. Raw bodies remain immutable even during fallback. If target content changed
since it was read, reconcile it before writing; do not overwrite concurrent work.

## Shell portability

Examples elsewhere use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` as command
notation. Replace the placeholder with the actual installed absolute path before
execution, and set the vault for the operation's scope. Do not execute literal
angle-bracket placeholders or assume a relative `scripts/` path means the plugin.

PowerShell (restore any prior environment value):

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki health failed' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

POSIX shell (one command's environment only):

```sh
WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault' node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
```

On Windows, use PowerShell or the Node wrapper for Obsidian; Git Bash can select
the GUI executable instead of `Obsidian.com` and return misleading empty output.
These reporting examples are read-only: do not open an operation or rebuild the
index merely to answer a question.

1	Read [access and host commands](access.md) before touching the vault. Also read for this operation: [maintenance](maintenance.md).
2	Load the rest only when this run reaches it — [operations](operations.md) only when you apply reclips or otherwise write; presenting the queue creates only local session state, not tracked content.
3	Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.
4	
5	## What this is for
6	Some links cannot be resolved by the pipeline: a 403, a paywalled SPA, an extraction that
7	landed on the wrong node, a PDF whose fonts decoded to gibberish. Printing those to the
8	terminal loses them the moment the scrollback scrolls. **Anything that needs the user's
9	eyes on a link belongs here**, not in console output.
10	
11	## Show the queue
12	```bash
13	node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/triage.mjs"
14	```
15	Prints one line of JSON: `{"type":"triage-ready","link":"http://localhost:PORT/?t=…","url":…}`
16	with counts. **Give the user `link`, not `url`.** Every route is behind a session token, and
17	`link` carries it — opening it once is the entire login, after which the browser holds an
18	HttpOnly cookie for 30 days. `url` is the clean form, for liveness checks and logs; on its
19	own it renders a 401. Hand over the link with a one-line summary of what is waiting, then
20	**end your turn**. They disposition in the browser; you read the results next turn.
21	
22	The server reuses one session directory per vault (`.wiki-master/triage-ui/`), so re-running
23	refreshes the open page rather than starting a second server. It idles out after 30 minutes.
24	
25	### Triaging from another machine
26	```bash
27	node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/triage.mjs" --remote
28	```
29	Default is loopback-only. `--remote` binds every interface and advertises a reachable
30	address instead of `0.0.0.0`, which no browser will open. Everything else is unchanged:
31	the same link, the same token, and uploads still land on the **server's** disk, which is
32	where `apply-reclips` will look for them.
33	
34	- **The token is re-printable, never memorized.** It lives in
35	  `.wiki-master/triage-ui/state/token` (gitignored, machine-local, `0600`) and is stable
36	  across restarts. If the user loses the link, read the file and rebuild it — do not
37	  regenerate it, or you invalidate the link they already have.
38	- **To rotate:** delete that file and re-run. Every existing session cookie stops working.
39	- **The port is remembered too** (`state/port`), because the cookie is scoped to
40	  `host:port` — a new port would silently force a fresh login every run.
41	- **Over a plain LAN the token crosses the wire in cleartext.** On a tailnet (WireGuard)
42	  or behind an HTTPS front that is fine; on an untrusted network, say so rather than
43	  assuming the user has thought about it.
44	- `WM_TRIAGE_URL_HOST` overrides the advertised hostname when the derived IP is not the
45	  one the user reaches the machine on.
46	
47	### Grouping by research topic
48	Rows are grouped by **kind** (kind decides which actions a row offers) and filtered by
49	**research topic** — the argument the user gave researcher discovery. A topic bar above the
50	groups scopes the whole queue to one run, because that is how these decisions are actually
51	made: "deal with what this topic research left behind", not "deal with all fidelity flags".
52	
53	Topic comes from `topic:` in a clipping's frontmatter, or from the triage log for issues
54	that never became a file. **It is only ever recorded going forward** — clippings made
55	before this existed, and any clip made outside a research run, group under
56	**Unattributed**. Say so if the user asks why a group is large; do not present
57	Unattributed as a defect to fix.
58	
59	When you summarize the queue for the user, lead with the topic breakdown when there is
60	more than one — it is the shape they will act on.
61	
62	## Read dispositions back
63	Dispositions append to `<vault>/.wiki-master/triage.jsonl` as
64	`{"t":"disposition","url":…,"kind":…,"disposition":…}`. Fold the log to get current state:
65	
66	```js
67	import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
68	const { loadIssueLog, openIssues } = await import(pathToFileURL('<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/lib/triage.mjs').href);
69	const stillOpen = openIssues(loadIssueLog(vaultPath));
70	```
71	
72	Then act on what the user chose. Starting the UI alone needs no content operation.
73	Before applying a disposition that changes tracked content or pipeline state, open
74	or reuse an operation; validate, log, commit, push and verify remote publication
75	through the completion contract. Handoffs such as ingest own their transaction.
76	
77	The dispositions a row offers depend on its kind. Clip failures (`failed`, `gone`,
78	`thin`, `wrong-node`, `blocked`) and `attention` rows offer `downloaded`,
79	`clipped-manually`, `retry`, `declined` and `ignore`. Fidelity rows offer
80	`acceptable`, `reclip`, `downloaded` and `quarantine`; an expiring decline offers
81	`keep-declined` and `reconsider`; the backlog offers `ingest` and `ignore`:
82	
83	| disposition | what you do |
84	|---|---|
85	| `clipped-manually` (shown as "clipped by hand") | confirm a clipping for that URL exists in `raw/clippings/`; if not, say so |
86	| `downloaded` | the user saved the source file themselves ("browse — clip this file"): `apply-reclips.mjs` re-clips an existing clipping from it; for a URL with no clipping yet, run the matching document clipper on the saved file with `--source="<url>"` and the run's `--topic`. A URL still in the decline log is skipped; add `--override-decline` when the decline is an automatic thin or wrong-node one (the clipper lifts it only after the clipping is written), or `--supersede-decline="<why>"` for any other. For a web page the user saved from a signed-in browser (a login, consent or age-gate row), supply it with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --from-file <path> --topic="<topic>"`; `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/decline.mjs" supersede "<url>" --reason "<why>"` ends a decline without clipping. `apply-reclips.mjs` does not re-clip a clipping with `extraction: manual` (it lists it as refused, not as a failure): to refresh a supplied page, run `clip.mjs "<url>" --from-file <path> --recapture` |
87	| `retry` | re-run `clip.mjs` for that URL — a transient failure may have cleared |
88	| `declined` | `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --decline="<reason>"` |
89	| `reconsider` | the decline is expiring and they want it re-evaluated — treat as a discovery candidate |
90	| `keep-declined` | re-record the decline to reset its TTL |
91	| `acceptable` | fidelity is good enough; no action beyond noting it |
92	| `reclip` | re-clip with the clipper that matches the file (`clip-pdf`, `clip-docx` or `clip-xlsx`) rather than the HTML clipper |
93	| `quarantine` | do not cite this source; note the restriction on any page that already does |
94	| `ingest` | follow [researcher ingestion](../../wiki-researcher/references/ingest.md) scoped to that source |
95	| `ignore` / `skip` | no action; the disposition itself is the record |
96	
97	## Queue something yourself
98	When a run surfaces a link only the user can settle, queue it rather than burying it in prose:
99	
100	```js
101	import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
102	const { recordIssue } = await import(pathToFileURL('<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/lib/triage.mjs').href);
103	recordIssue(vaultPath, { url, kind: 'attention', reason: 'why this needs a human', topic });
104	```
105	
106	Pass `topic` whenever the item came out of a research run — it is what puts the row in
107	that run's group instead of Unattributed. Omit it when there is no run behind the item;
108	an invented topic is worse than none, because it files the row under a heading the user
109	has already worked through.
110	
111	Kinds: `failed` · `gone` · `thin` · `wrong-node` · `blocked` · `fidelity` · `attention`.
112	
113	`failed` and `gone` ask opposite things of the user: `failed` means *try this again, by
114	hand or from a signed-in browser*; `gone` means *stop trying — the page is a 404, or
115	redirects onto an error page, so find another source or drop the claim*. Never file a
116	dead link as `failed`; a row nobody can action is a row that stays in the queue forever.
117	
118	## Guardrails
119	- **The log is append-only.** Never rewrite `triage.jsonl` — dispositions are appended and
120	  state is folded at read time. Two sessions share one vault routinely, and a
121	  read-modify-write on a shared file loses the other session's entries silently.
122	- **A recurrence reopens an issue.** A failure seen again after disposition is news, not
123	  history — do not suppress it.
124	- **Transient failures are not declines.** A 403 is a fact about one fetch; a decline is a
125	  judgment. Queuing a transient failure as a decline buries a recoverable source under a
126	  180-day TTL.
127	- **Report counts honestly.** The backlog group is capped for display and says so. Never
128	  present a truncated list as the whole set.
129

|---|---|
| `clipped-manually` (shown as "clipped by hand") | confirm a clipping for that URL exists in `raw/clippings/`; if not, say so |
| `downloaded` | the user saved the source file themselves ("browse — clip this file"): `apply-reclips.mjs` re-clips an existing clipping from it; for a URL with no clipping yet, run the matching document clipper on the saved file with `--source="<url>"` and the run's `--topic`. A URL still in the decline log is skipped; add `--override-decline` when the decline is an automatic thin or wrong-node one (the clipper lifts it only after the clipping is written), or `--supersede-decline="<why>"` for any other. For a web page the user saved from a signed-in browser (a login, consent or age-gate row), supply it with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --from-file <path> --topic="<topic>"`; `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/decline.mjs" supersede "<url>" --reason "<why>"` ends a decline without clipping. `apply-reclips.mjs` does not re-clip a clipping with `extraction: manual` (it lists it as refused, not as a failure): to refresh a supplied page, run `clip.mjs "<url>" --from-file <path> --recapture` |
| `retry` | re-run `clip.mjs` for that URL — a transient failure may have cleared |
| `declined` | `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --decline="<reason>"` |
| `reconsider` | the decline is expiring and they want it re-evaluated — treat as a discovery candidate |
| `keep-declined` | re-record the decline to reset its TTL |
| `acceptable` | fidelity is good enough; no action beyond noting it |
| `reclip` | re-clip with the clipper that matches the file (`clip-pdf`, `clip-docx` or `clip-xlsx`) rather than the HTML clipper |
| `quarantine` | do not cite this source; note the restriction on any page that already does |
| `ingest` | follow [researcher ingestion](../../wiki-researcher/references/ingest.md) scoped to that source |
| `ignore` / `skip` | no action; the disposition itself is the record |

## Queue something yourself
When a run surfaces a link only the user can settle, queue it rather than burying it in prose:

```js
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
const { recordIssue } = await import(pathToFileURL('<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/lib/triage.mjs').href);
recordIssue(vaultPath, { url, kind: 'attention', reason: 'why this needs a human', topic });
```

Pass `topic` whenever the item came out of a research run — it is what puts the row in
that run's group instead of Unattributed. Omit it when there is no run behind the item;
an invented topic is worse than none, because it files the row under a heading the user
has already worked through.

Kinds: `failed` · `gone` · `thin` · `wrong-node` · `blocked` · `fidelity` · `attention`.

`failed` and `gone` ask opposite things of the user: `failed` means *try this again, by
hand or from a signed-in browser*; `gone` means *stop trying — the page is a 404, or
redirects onto an error page, so find another source or drop the claim*. Never file a
dead link as `failed`; a row nobody can action is a row that stays in the queue forever.

## Guardrails
- **The log is append-only.** Never rewrite `triage.jsonl` — dispositions are appended and
  state is folded at read time. Two sessions share one vault routinely, and a
  read-modify-write on a shared file loses the other session's entries silently.
- **A recurrence reopens an issue.** A failure seen again after disposition is news, not
  history — do not suppress it.
- **Transient failures are not declines.** A 403 is a fact about one fetch; a decline is a
  judgment. Queuing a transient failure as a decline buries a recoverable source under a
  180-day TTL.
- **Report counts honestly.** The backlog group is capped for display and says so. Never
  present a truncated list as the whole set.
